title: Salt and Sigil
premise: Marguerite Sterling, the crown's food-taster, has spent years dosing himself with poison until his body became a ledger of survival — and by night he keeps accounts for the Gilded Ledger, a guild that trades in impossible things: borrowed years, smuggled names, doors between realms. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Marguerite discovers the guild's oldest contract — a covenant between the human court and the drowned realm beneath the salt marshes — was broken decades ago, and its breach is now poisoning both worlds. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and drawn to Wren, a sigil-scribe from the drowned realm sent to retrieve him, Marguerite must choose between the crown that owns his life and the stranger who makes him want one of his own. In the end he reforges the covenant with his own poisoned blood as ink, paying the price of survival by surrendering his immunity — and choosing love and mortality over the safety of being untouchable.
about_author: Isandro Okafor is a former archivist who writes fantasy about ledgers, debts, and the people caught between them. He lives near a tidal estuary and claims the salt air edits his prose.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A morning at court: Marguerite tastes the king's soup, detects hemlock, and saves a duke while feeling nothing himself. That night he balances the Gilded Ledger's impossible accounts. The beat establishes his numb competence and the quiet horror of a body that no longer belongs to him.

chapters.title: A Courier at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A bleeding stranger collapses in the guild's counting-house, pressing a salt-crusted map into Marguerite's hands and whispering 'the covenant broke' before dying. Guild enforcers arrive minutes later; Marguerite lies for the first time in his careful life. Beat: fear and the first crack in obedience.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Reading hidden entries, Marguerite learns the guild brokered the covenant between the crown and the drowned realm — and someone erased forty years of payments. Enforcers burn the counting-house; he flees with the map. Beat: betrayal, loss, the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Scribe in the Reeds
chapters.summary: POV alternating Marguerite/Wren. Following the map into the marshes, Marguerite is ambushed by salt-wraiths and saved by Wren, a scribe whose skin bears living sigils. She needs the map's bearer; he needs answers. Beat: wary alliance, first spark of recognition between two owned people.

chapters.title: Doors Between Realms
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren leads Marguerite through a drowned door into the sunken realm, revealing what the broken covenant has cost: her people are dissolving into brine as their names are unmade. She confesses she was sent to retrieve — or kill — him. Beat: wonder shadowed by distrust and rising stakes.

chapters.title: The King's Poisoner
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Captured by crown agents, Marguerite discovers the king himself ordered the covenant broken, feeding the drowned realm's stolen years to extend his reign. Offered wealth and freedom to surrender the map, Marguerite refuses — and tastes real fear for the first time. Beat: moral clarity purchased at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Salt in the Blood
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Fleeing together, Wren and Marguerite shelter in a ruined chapel where she teaches him sigil-craft using his own poisoned blood as ink. They admit what they feel; duty on both sides forbids it. Beat: tenderness against inevitability, the theme of love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: The Price of Immunity
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The guild's master reveals the truth: Marguerite's immunity was bought with the drowned realm's stolen names — he is the covenant's breach made flesh. To reforge it, the taster must give back every dose he ever survived. Beat: devastating identity reversal; the survivor learns he is the debt.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV alternating. At the drowned throne during the king's assault, Marguerite writes the new covenant in his own blood while Wren holds the door against royal soldiers. Each stroke returns his immunity and returns pain, memory, mortality. He signs; the realms lock; the king falls. Beat: climax — sacrifice as choice, not sentence.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Weeks later: the guild reformed under honest accounting, the drowned realm breathing again. Marguerite, now able to be hurt, chooses to stay at the threshold as its keeper — with Wren beside him. Final beat: resolution — survival's price paid, identity chosen, love kept.
